title: fix(telegram): preserve webhook delivery on 2026.9.6 hosts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes separately installed Telegram plugin loading and webhook listeners on the declared OpenClaw 2026.9.6 host, which predates the newer Doctor helpers and Gateway-owned legacy listeners.

## User Impact

Existing 9.6 webhook endpoints retain their per-account listener and durable-before-ack behavior. Capable hosts keep Gateway-owned listeners. Older hosts require distinct legacy ports across accounts and display migration guidance through their supported warning output; these limitations are documented. No host-floor, config schema, dependency, or public SDK change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The package builder carries named canonical helpers required by supported hosts. Pure normalization and path-prefix helpers move out of modules that also own caches or account metadata; their behavior is unchanged. Telegram also carries the canonical per-turn preview lifecycle required by its delivery code, while error formatting remains bound to the installed host’s redaction owner. Other plugins keep their host lifecycle factory. These package bindings retire when the declared host floor includes the required contracts. The assertion allowance only shrinks from seven to five after removing unnecessary casts.

Telegram selects the listener owner through the existing host capability. On 9.6, the predecessor's per-account server uses the current authentication and durable admission handler. Shutdown closes admission first, allows bot/transport/ingress and accepted-write cleanup, then joins the same listener closure before reporting stopped. There is no second listener on capable hosts, independent shutdown manager, or new timeout.

## Evidence

Causal checks reproduce the original absent listener, invisible old-host Doctor guidance, and missing exports in native ESM/CJS packages. An independent review also caught an active-request shutdown ordering defect; the added real HTTP regression failed before the ordering repair and passes after it, including resumed-body rejection, no admission after stop, and final port release.

The final adapter suite passes 8/8; Doctor checks pass 41/41, packaging checks 26/26, and the pure migration/path/mention owner suites pass. The lifecycle follow-up also passes 18 canonical lifecycle, 10 Telegram final-outcome, and nine draft-finalization cases. Its original native ESM/CJS package regressions fail on the missing lifecycle method; repaired packages preserve accepted delivery receipts and use the host error formatter. Selected formatting, strict types, lint, boundaries, storage/auth/webhook/import guards and ratchets pass. The prior full-PR review and fresh incremental P0–P2 review of the lifecycle/test follow-up are clean, with unchanged source applicability recorded. Actual package proof at `cac6c76ec652eae4f1aee411e6ea80cdb2e5a7b4` passes published 9.6 CLI installation, complete plugin registration, Doctor migration, and native `/help` delivery through the plugin-owned legacy listener. After a cold restart over the same state, delivery through the Gateway route also passes. A separately installed current candidate passes both phases with Gateway-owned legacy forwarding. Runtime cells activate the complete package through the actual host’s supported bundled-plugin directory override; ordinary CLI installation and full registration are separate checks. Both hosts reject missing/wrong secrets, acknowledge durable admission, complete and retire the payload through the real queue owner, preserve completed rows across restart, and join shutdown with both ports released. All original host members remain unchanged except the documented pending-lifecycle marker consumed by the shipped CLI. Canonical build and the qualified Telegram entrypoint profiler pass. These are controlled Bot API callbacks, not real Telegram/Test Server delivery or model inference.

Real Telegram Test Server delivery also passes on the immutable final-head package. [Package Acceptance 36354939833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36354939833) built source `3fa57d7ac0222ed8e3c7f5c1870dd6bd81815943` and passed native `/help`, including `/new` and `/commands`. [Telegram E2E 36356765627](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36356765627) consumed that same core tarball (`b282381ba1c265dd51b890e1b9c04647790fc82a916177cab2dd9aee71e3beb0`) and its source-matched Codex plugin registry. The real Test Server user observed detailed progress change from commentary-only to `Exec running`, then to `Exec`, preserving commentary through both message edits before exactly one separate final reply. The quiet case hid tool rows and also delivered one final. Each case recorded two successful mock-provider requests and one correlated successful exec result, with no progress after final. Both selected scenarios passed without retries or skipped cases. The maintained runner completed its awaited Gateway, transport, proxy, and credential-lease cleanup before publishing the terminal results; no independent broker-release or signal ledger is claimed.

This combines actual published-host HTTP listener/authentication/lifetime proof with real Telegram payload, delivery, and per-turn behavior on the current artifact. The direct old-host Test Server webhook cell remains unrun: the live lane uses the maintained polling transport, and it does not establish public webhook reachability, old-host live delivery, live model inference, typing, or deletion. That boundary is intentional in the maintainer review disposition of the broader ClawSweeper request. The compact help runtime receipt leaves source/package fields null; immutable artifact verification and installed CLI attribution provide that identity, and no measured help provider-request count is claimed.

The earlier `3c8a757` package proof reached admission but failed native delivery at `beginFinalDelivery`; its failure is retained. The lifecycle follow-up repairs that demonstrated mismatch. The initial current-host fixture-ordering failure and its separately reviewed recovery also remain recorded.

The existing 111-case webhook suite recorded HTTP timing failures. A separate fixture-only repair, [#159828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159828), restores the production monitor's awaited durable-state preparation before those lower-level tests begin their unchanged request budgets. Its causal controls and repeat qualification are separate evidence; that patch is not included here and the original failures remain retained. The unique initial-POST shutdown AbortError was not directly reproduced, so it is not presented as independently proven unrelated.

Initial CI at `3c8a757` was cancelled after two core-fixture failures: an unreachable ACP phase comparison and a Gateway recovery assertion that ran before async settlement. Both are repaired independently by [#159836](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159836), which is present on current main. The original logs remain retained; final-head [CI 36351168747](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36351168747) passes at `3fa57d7ac0222ed8e3c7f5c1870dd6bd81815943`.

CI at `cac6c76` then caught a missing source-inventory entry for the extracted HTTP path helper. Follow-up `3fa57d7ac0222ed8e3c7f5c1870dd6bd81815943` adds that one entry; all 16 existing wrapper-extraction tests and a fresh scoped review pass. Every other tracked file is identical to `cac6c76`. The build and actual-package cells remain explicitly pinned to `cac6c76`; the same final-head CI also passes for the inventory change.

<details>
<summary>Changed-test runtime and proof boundaries</summary>

- Final single-worker adapter file: 93.498 seconds process wall time, 8 passing cases. The shutdown regression synchronizes with an existing cleanup phase and checks a refused new connection before releasing the held request.
- Doctor host-floor file: 108.017 seconds process wall time, 2 passing cases. Combined Doctor verification later passed 41 cases.
- Final package-builder file: 82.146 seconds process wall time, 26 passing cases. The earlier 24-case measurement was 303.274 seconds, including 231.3 seconds of canonical runtime preparation; these different preparation states are not a performance comparison.

These files exercise real HTTP lifecycle, Doctor warning generation, and executable package boundaries. Compiler/import preparation dominates the long commands; no timeout or assertion was weakened. The initial Doctor measurement used the retained isolated preparation environment. That environment was removed from the later ordinary webhook/Doctor runs; the earlier profile-related port failures and the normal-environment sibling comparison remain separately identified. CI timings will be recorded when available.

The installed-host Gateway proof uses a controlled Bot API fixture with injected HTTP callbacks and real storage/native command dispatch. The separate final-head live lane uses real Telegram Test Server polling and preserves observed message revisions. Neither is labeled a direct public Telegram webhook round trip.

</details>
